basis.note: No published standard was read. Topics follow an introductory modern-physics chapter (OpenStax University Physics vol. 3 ch. 11, chapter title from memory); the objective list is a house decision.

big_ideas.title: Twelve fermions and four forces
big_ideas.text: Six quarks and six leptons in three generations, each with an antiparticle, interacting by exchanging photons, W and Z bosons and gluons.

big_ideas.title: What can happen is what conserves everything
big_ideas.text: Charge, baryon number and each lepton number balance in every reaction; energy decides whether an allowed reaction can actually go.

practices.title: Compute
practices.text: Carry a charge, a quantum number or an energy to a value.

practices.title: Decide
practices.text: Say whether a reaction is allowed and which interaction is responsible.

los.do: Find the charge of a hadron from its quark content.
ek: u, c, t: +2/3; d, s, b: −1/3; antiquarks opposite.

los.do: Classify a hadron as a baryon, an antibaryon or a meson.
ek: Three quarks, three antiquarks, or a quark and an antiquark.

los.do: Name the carrier of each interaction and the interaction behind a given process.
ek: Photon, W and Z, gluon; only the weak force changes flavour.

los.do: Check charge, baryon number and lepton numbers in a reaction or decay.
ek: Each balances separately; electron and muon lepton numbers are counted apart.

los.do: Convert a mass to a rest energy and find a pair-production threshold.
ek: 931.5 MeV per u; a pair costs twice the rest energy.

los.do: Calculate a Lorentz factor and a dilated lifetime or range.
ek: γ = 1/√(1 − v²/c²); lab lifetime = γ × rest lifetime.
